In 2025, Dash Living was acquired by Rava Partners, the real estate private equity arm under Hillhouse, further strengthening its growth trajectory and regional expansion plans. With more than US$1.1Billion assets under management on a committed and deployed basis, over 2,000 rooms across 43 locations currently in our portfolio, Dash creates a global accommodation community through sharing economies, tech, and unique member experiences, empowering living in a connected world. Dash Living manages assets on behalf of renowned real estate investment managers such as BlackRock, Greystar, Schroders, PGIM Real Estate, Hines, and more. ROLE SUMMARY Dash Living is the leading hotel and coliving provider in the Asia Pacific. Our mission is to provide affordable and flexible rental solutions for today’s youth. Our culture is entrepreneurial and teamwork-oriented, and one where we encourage creative input. We are looking for a candidate with product management experience as well as IT skills to further develop user engagement within the Dash community, as well as assist in scaling up existing software to meet new workflow demands. The successful candidate will ensure that PMS, POS, Wi-Fi, guest-facing technology, security systems, and back-office systems remain highly available, secure, and aligned with business and guest expectations. WHAT YOU’LL DO Serve as the first point of contact for IT support in Japan, providing basic troubleshooting and resolution for hardware, software, and operating system issues (Windows/macOS) on staff devices. Provide day-to-day technical support for core company applications, including Google Workspace (Gmail, Calendar, Drive), Slack, and other business-critical tools, covering account setup, access, and troubleshooting. Manage user onboarding and offboarding, including account creation, access rights, and device provisioning and recovery. Configure, monitor, and maintain network equipment and firewalls, ensuring stable and secure office connectivity for 100+ users. Deploy and manage endpoint security solutions, implement patch management, and maintain firewall rules and VPN access in line with company cybersecurity policies. Maintain strong information security awareness and ensure IT operations comply with Japan's Act on the Protection of Personal Information (APPI), safeguarding staff and guest personal data. Administer CCTV and door access control systems, including user permissions, access reviews, and audit trails. Manage and maintain high-performance guest and staff Wi-Fi networks. Oversee data security for all software systems (PMS, POS, keycards, etc.) and support data backup and recovery. Manage IT assets, including inventory tracking and vendor coordination, and keep IT documentation up to date. Manage the procurement of computers and other IT equipment, from requirement gathering and specification selection to vendor sourcing, purchasing, and initial setup, in line with company standards and budget. Coordinate with the global IT team on cloud infrastructure, security incidents, and disaster recovery, escalating complex issues as needed. Collaborate with operations and other departments to identify and implement technology improvements that support business goals. WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR At least 3 years of IT support or helpdesk experience Hands-on experience configuring network devices and firewalls, and managing a company network supporting 100+ users Solid troubleshooting skills across Windows and macOS operating systems and common business applications Good information security awareness, including endpoint protection, patch management, and firewall configuration Familiarity with CCTV and door access control systems and their permission management Familiarity with Microsoft 365, Active Directory/Entra ID, and cloud platforms (Azure, AWS) is a plus Fluent in both Japanese and English to communicate effectively with local vendors, staff, and the global team; proficiency in Chinese is a plus. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to lead cross-departmental collaboration A strong sense of responsibility, initiative, and eagerness to learn Relevant certifications are highly desirable: ITIL, CompTIA A+/Network+, CCNA, or equivalent Bachelor's degree holder or above in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related discipline Must be based in Tokyo, Japan WHAT WE OFFER Opportunity to learn and explore new markets 5-day work week and a competitive salary package with a discretionary bonus A fun, dynamic, and friendly startup environment A generous number of vacation days each year Personal Information Collection Statement-Applicants’ personal information will be used for recruitment and employment matters only; information will be kept in strict confidence; information of unsuccessful applicants will be shredded after the recruitment process; subject to provisions under the Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance, applicants have the right to access and make corrections to their personal data.

review_candidates.title: Senior Platform Engineer
review_candidates.description: About the Role Our world-leading Time & Frequency department are seeking a Senior Platform Engineer with experience in VMware technologies, VDI platforms, automation, systems administration, and infrastructure resilience. This is an exceptional opportunity to join the global authority in precision timing at a defining moment for UK digital infrastructure. Backed by a government investment of £180 million in the National Timing Centre (NTC) programme, we are developing a world-first resilient time distribution capability that will provide industry with a robust complement to satellite systems (such as GPS) – which are increasingly vulnerable to disruption from solar storms, jamming and spoofing. This will underpin essential services, including Telecommunications, Online banking, Emergency response, Transport networks, and Wider digital and data-driven operations. Together, these services form the backbone of modern society - and your leadership will help ensure they remain secure, reliable and robust even if global navigation satellite systems fail. Key Responsibilities As a Senior Platform Engineer specialising in Virtualisation, Windows, and Security, you will support and maintain critical infrastructure across multiple customer environments, with a strong focus on automation and DevOps practices. Working as part of a specialist team, you will design, deploy, administer, and optimise virtualisation platforms, end-user computing solutions, servers, and supporting infrastructure services, including orchestration services (Kubernetes) running on virtual platforms. Key responsibilities include: Administering, maintaining, and optimising VMware vCenter and vSAN environments. Supporting and developing VDI platforms. Managing Windows Server environments, including Active Directory, Trusts, DNS, Group Policy, PKI, certificate services, and security hardening. Designing, implementing, and supporting resilient, highly available infrastructure solutions, while troubleshooting complex infrastructure, platform, and network issues. Delivering upgrades, migrations, patching, and lifecycle management activities. Developing automation and orchestration capabilities using scripting and Infrastructure as Code (IaC). Supporting enterprise security initiatives, including privileged access management, monitoring, logging, and data protection. Producing technical documentation, operational procedures, and support runbooks. Contributing to disaster recovery, business continuity, and redundancy planning. Travelling to sites as required to support deployment, implementation, and operational activities. About You Essential Criteria To be successful in this role, you will have: Experience designing, deploying, administering, and supporting VMware environments, including ESXi, vCenter, and vSAN. Experience administering Windows Server in enterprise environments, including the design, implementation, and support of Microsoft services such as Active Directory, Group Policy, and PKI. Experience supporting VDI environments. Strong scripting and automation skills using one or more of PowerShell, Ansible, Bash, Python, or Terraform. Experience designing, implementing, maintaining, and supporting secure, resilient, and highly available systems. Experience producing technical documentation, operational procedures/runbooks, and implementation plans. Strong stakeholder management, communication, and engagement skills. Demonstrable experience in a senior infrastructure, platform engineering, systems administration, or technical consultancy role. Relevant certifications in VMware, Omnissa, Microsoft, or automation technologies are desirable. Desirable Criteria Knowledge of Linux operating systems, with a willingness to further develop skills in Linux & related Linux tooling. Experience with Kubernetes and containerised platforms. Experience supporting infrastructure in regulated, public sector, financial, or security-conscious environments. We actively recruit citizens of all backgrounds, but the nature of our work in specific departments means that nationality, residency and security requirements can be more tightly defined than others. You will be asked about this throughout the recruitment process. To work at NPL, you will need to obtain BPSS security clearance. However, to work in this role in the Time & Frequency department, you will need to have an SC clearance with no restrictions, or you must have the ability to obtain an SC clearance. About Us The National Physical Laboratory (NPL) is a world-leading centre of excellence that provides cutting-edge measurement science, engineering and technology to underpin prosperity and quality of life in the UK. Find out more about what it is like working here - The measure of us - Overview NPL and DSIT have strong commitments to diversity and equality of opportunity, and welcome applications from candidates irrespective of their background, gender, race, sexual orientation, religion, or age, providing they meet the required criteria. Applications from women, disabled and black, Asian and minority ethnic candidates in particular are encouraged. All disabled candidates (as defined by the Equality Act 2010) who satisfy the minimum criteria for the role will be guaranteed an interview under the Disability Confident Scheme. At NPL, we believe our success is a result of the diversity and talent of our people. We strive to nurture and respect individuals to ensure everyone feels valued by treating everyone on the basis of their own individual merits and abilities regardless of their own or perceived identity, as part of our commitment to diversity & inclusion, we ensure we’re creating an environment where all our colleagues feel supported and welcome. More about this on our Diversity & Inclusion page. We are committed to the health and well-being of our employees. Flexible working and social activities are embedded in our culture to create a positive work-life balance, along with a broad range of rewards, benefits and recognition. Our values are at the heart of what we do, and they shape the way we interact, develop our people and celebrate success. To ensure everyone has an equal chance, we’re always willing to make reasonable adjustments to the recruitment process. If you would like to discuss, please contact us.

review_candidates.title: Senior Staff AI Infrastructure Engineer
review_candidates.description: AI ACCELERATOR Most diseases are still poorly understood at a biological level. Despite decades of research, the causal mechanisms driving many conditions remain unclear, limiting our ability to identify the right targets, design the right interventions and bring the right medicines to patients. The AI Accelerator exists to change that. Based in London and sitting within Computational Innovation (@computationalinnovation), a global organisation spanning computational biology, human genetics, data excellence and AI, the Accelerator’s mission is to build production-quality AI capabilities that deepen our understanding of disease biology and increase probability of success. We do this by applying neural-based methods across the biomedical data landscape to integrate heterogeneous, multimodal data sources, infer biological relationships and embed causal thinking into what we build. The goal is not just to predict but to explain and understand why disease occurs. It could be electronic health records and medical imaging to support patient segmentation. It could be ‘omics data to identify novel therapeutic targets. It could be predicting transcriptional change for a given disease-causing variant. It could be simulating the effect of modulating a target of interest. AI Infrastructure underpins the success of the AI Accelerator: the scale, speed and cost of every model trained or served rests on the compute, storage and platform substrate deployed. This includes getting the best from existing on-prem capabilities as well as securing best-value cloud capabilities. THE POSITION We are seeking a senior leader of AI Infrastructure to join Computational Innovation’s AI Accelerator. In this role, you will own the technical infrastructure strategy for the AI Accelerator, ensuring the unit has the compute, storage and platform infrastructure it needs to train, fine-tune and serve biomedical foundation models at scale. You will lead the architecture, standards and practices for the compute and platform substrate on which the other teams depend, working wider CI data teams and IT, as well as cloud providers, to ensure that our AI scientists and ML teams get the best from all available infrastructure. This is a technical leadership role that requires deep technical expertise and relationship building. You will be a senior member of the AI Enablement leadership team, contributing to the team's overall direction alongside the Senior Staff Data Engineer and Senior Staff MLOps Engineer. This is a unique opportunity to be part of a critical strategic initiative for a pharmaceutical company that invests heavily in research and development to discover and develop innovative therapies that can improve and extend lives in areas of high unmet medical need. Key Responsibilities Own, define and evolve a wholistic, multi-layer reference architecture spanning storage, compute, environments and platform stack, making appropriate use of vendor/integrator design patterns. Set the technical direction, strategy and roadmap for AI infrastructure, aligned to the various AI Enablement roadmaps and to portfolio/research priorities. Partner with Data Excellence to further development BI's Trusted Research Environment (TRE), ensuring the TRE supports secure, compliant AI workloads on sensitive data and evolves to meet the AI Accelerator’s needs. In partnership with IT, shape the evolution of existing enterprise infrastructure to support large-scale AI and ensure best-value services while designing for portability. Establish ways of working, onboard and mentor other team members, and act as a senior escalation point for complex AI Infrastructure problems. Requirements PhD or MSc with equivalent experience in a STEM subject. Extensive experience as a senior staff-level infrastructure, platform or systems engineer for compute-intensive workloads, including setting architecture, standards and technical direction for a team or function. Deep expertise across the AI compute infrastructure stack: high-performance and GPU compute, storage and file systems, networking, container platforms and orchestration (e.g. Kubernetes), environment provisioning and infrastructure-as-code (e.g. Terraform). Significant experience with hybrid on-prem/cloud architectures, including right-sizing, cost optimisation and designing for portability to avoid lock-in. Expertise in providing infrastructure that enables large-scale AI workloads, including distributed training at scale. Understanding of security, access control, resilience/continuity and systems-operation rigour (ITIL or equivalent service management). Strong collaboration and influencing skills across technical and non-technical stakeholders; ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly and to mediate competing requirements. Experience mentoring or technically leading engineers and setting engineering principles. This is a hybrid role with approximately 4 days a week in the office. WHY THIS IS A GREAT PLACE TO WORK Boehringer Ingelheim has been recognised as a Top Employer in the UK, demonstrating our commitment to building an exceptional workplace through strong people practices and supportive HR policies. To learn more about why BI is a great place to work, visit: https://www.boehringer-ingelheim.co.uk/careers/uk-careers/why-great-place-work Our Company Boehringer Ingelheim is a biopharmaceutical company active in both human and animal health. As one of the industry's top investors in research and development, the company focuses on developing innovative therapies that can improve and extend lives in areas of high unmet medical need. Independent since its foundation in 1885, Boehringer takes a long-term perspective, embedding sustainability along the entire value chain. Our approximately 54,300 employees serve over 130 markets to build a healthier and more sustainable tomorrow. Learn more at www.boehringer-ingelheim.com. Why Boehringer Ingelheim? With us, you can develop your own path in a company with a culture that knows our differences are our strengths - and break new ground in the drive to make millions of lives better. Here, your development is our priority. Supporting you to build a career as part of a workplace that is independent, authentic and bold, while tackling challenging work in a respectful and friendly environment where everyone is valued and welcomed. Alongside, you have access to programs and groups that ensure your health and wellbeing are looked after - as we make major investments to drive global accessibility to healthcare. By being part of a team that is constantly innovating, you'll be helping to transform lives for generations. Want to learn more? Visit https://www.boehringer-ingelheim.com

As a member of the Executive Committee, the Chief People Officer will play a pivotal role in shaping the future of one of the world's most recognisable and trusted organisations. As Chief People Officer, you will lead the BBC's people and culture agenda, driving organisational transformation as the business accelerates its evolution into a digital-first media organisation. You will help build a future-ready workforce, strengthen organisational effectiveness, and ensure the BBC continues to attract, develop and empower exceptional talent in an increasingly competitive and fast-changing landscape. Combining strategic influence with operational leadership, the successful candidate will lead large-scale cultural and organisational change, helping the BBC navigate an evolving funding and media environment while preserving the creative excellence, innovation and public service values that make it unique. Your Key Responsibilities And Impact KEY PRIORITIES Re-shaping the organisation to achieve a leaner BBC with an effective, agile, and process-light operating model and working culture that is fit for the future and embeds creative and editorial excellence. Leading industrial and employee relations strategy through enterprise-wide transformation, building constructive, trusted relationships with recognised trade unions and employee representatives, to enable sustainable organisational change. Setting a path for how people can both start a career in the creative industry as well as develop exciting career and development pathways at the BBC. Supporting the continued alignment of the talent pipeline to ensure succession, retention, attraction, diversity and inclusion objectives are achieved. Upholding a culture that is values-led, focused on maintaining the highest creativity and editorial excellence, and which reinforces the strategy to create a modern BBC. Key Responsibilities Will Include Lead the people strategy underpinning a multi-year transformation programme, reshaping the organisation's operating model and workforce to deliver substantial cost efficiencies, organisational simplification and enhanced organisational effectiveness. Drive cultural transformation across the organisation, embedding a high-performance, accountable and values-led culture that supports innovation, agility, editorial and operational excellence. Design and execute workforce restructuring and organisational redesign initiatives, including the delivery of significant headcount reduction programmes, ensuring business continuity and alignment with long-term strategic priorities with a view to re-organising how the corporation operates, as opposed to consistent restructuring programmes. Provide executive leadership of employee relations across a highly unionised and publicly scrutinised environment, leading collective consultation processes, workforce engagement and negotiations with recognised trade unions and employee representatives. Partner with the Director-General, Board and Executive Committee to define the future workforce required to support the BBC’s strategic evolution, including workforce planning, capability assessment and skills transformation. Lead enterprise-wide change management activity, ensuring leaders are equipped to communicate, implement and sustain large-scale organisational change while maintaining colleague engagement and performance. ARE YOU THE RIGHT CANDIDATE? The BBC’s next CPO will be a transformational, Board credible executive, adept at navigating complex, high-scrutiny organisations either as the sitting CPO, or as a strong number two with sufficient Executive and Board level experience and ready for a step up. The successful candidate must bring the following expertise. Key Experience The Successful Candidate Will Demonstrate Enterprise Transformation – has led large-scale organisational transformation, including operating model redesign, strategic workforce planning, technology-enabled change and cultural evolution, delivering sustainable improvements in organisational effectiveness, agility and performance. Executive and Board Credibility – has advised CEOs, Executive Committees and Boards on sensitive People, Succession, Reward, reputational and governance matters, with an ability to coach and influence senior peers strategically and effectively. Commercial and Operational Excellence – works closely with Leadership Teams and Boards to align people strategy with organisational priorities, delivering measurable business outcomes through disciplined execution, operational excellence, stakeholder engagement and technology enabled solutions. Industrial and Employee Relations – has led industrial and employee relations strategy in complex, highly unionised and publicly scrutinised environments, building constructive partnerships with recognised trade unions, employee representatives and external stakeholders. Demonstrates the ability to navigate significant organisational change, manage workforce and reputational risk, and secure sustainable outcomes that balance organisational priorities with colleague experience. Leadership of a Modern People Function – has transformed People functions through technology, service redesign, data and analytics, operational efficiency, improved employee experience and stronger business insight. Brings experience of major HR technology implementation and building a culture of AI experimentation and functional cost management. Key Behaviours and Characteristics Strong interpersonal, coaching and listening skills with an ability to build trusted relationships and communicate effectively across all levels of a complex organisation. Action-oriented and pragmatic, able to translate strategy into execution and deliver outcomes in a fast-moving, operationally complex environment. Exceptional judgement and credibility, with a strong track record of identifying, developing and enabling talented leaders and high-performing teams. High levels of empathy, self-awareness and situational judgement, with the ability to influence, engage and bring others with them through periods of uncertainty and change. Enterprise thinker, able to balance immediate priorities with long-term organisational outcomes and navigate competing stakeholder interests effectively. Curious and externally focused, bringing insight from leading organisations and adapting emerging trends, technologies and ways of working to organisational needs.
